loquacious

loh-KWAY-shus · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Loquacious is tending to talk a great deal, in a fluent and confident way.

The loquacious podcast host could turn a single question into a fascinating twenty-minute answer.

Worked Example

Even the shyest guests on her show became loquacious once she asked about their childhood pets.

Loquacious emphasizes fluent, confident, often skillful talkativeness -- a more even-handed or even admiring quality than garrulous.

Your Turn

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

voluble: Voluble means talking easily, rapidly, and at length -- once started, the words simply keep coming. Loquacious covers the same steady flow but adds polish: a loquacious speaker sounds fluent and confident, while a voluble one may just be unstoppable.

garrulous: Garrulous means talkative in a rambling, tiresome way, running on about unimportant things after listeners stop caring. Loquacious is the kinder cousin: it names the same love of talk, but fluent and confident, and it can even sound admiring.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

taciturn: reluctant to speak much

laconic: using very few words

Where it sits · how smoothly the speech flows — talkative → loquacious → eloquent

talkative vs. loquacious: Talkative is the everyday, plain word; loquacious adds a sense of fluent, confident skill in speaking.

eloquent vs. loquacious: Eloquent goes a step beyond loquacious in polish: a loquacious speaker keeps easy, flowing talk coming, while an eloquent one shapes it into speech so graceful and moving it can sway a room.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — loqu

root — loqu: to speak (Latin (loqui))

suffix — -acious

suffix — -acious: full of, inclined to (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: loqu- ('to speak') + -acious ('full of, inclined to') together mean 'full of speaking' -- fluently talkative.

Use the root in a new word: eloquent

Use the root in a new word: eloquent: Eloquent shares the same Latin root loqui ('to speak'), joined here with the prefix ex- ('out').
